messages:
Maria Chen: Quick Q — should we reopen RICE scoring for Predictive Cache this quarter? Customer asks + measurable perf wins, but scope is fuzzy. Thinking: big impact if we nail it, but might be a multi-sprint lift.
Samir Patel: +1 to re-evaluate. My concern is effort estimate variance. We should consider slicing: core prefix cache (low effort) vs full KV cache + invalidation (high effort).
Alex Rivera: Need numbers to make any decent RICE change. Can we pull: traffic hit-rate for common prefixes, current p50/p95 for hit vs miss, and top customers affected?
Kim Nguyen: Also define launch criteria up front. Suggested gates: 1) stable correctness on devbench, 2) <10% p50 regressions on canary, 3) end-to-end latency savings >= 15% for cache-hit flows. If we don't commit to gates we'll scope-creep.
Jordan Lee: Sequencing idea: ship a "prefetch + prefix cache" beta to 10% traffic (canary) — gives early impact data with small effort. Then iterate to full predictive KV if metrics justify. This buys us both speed and de-risking.
Maria Chen: I like the canary-first approach. For RICE recalc we need: Reach (requests/min affected), Impact (expected uplift on revenue or latency), Confidence (data-backed), Effort (dev+infra weeks). Can someone draft a quick back-of-envelope?
Samir Patel: Quick back-of-envelope: Reach ~ 30k requests/day for cacheable paths, Impact = 0.25 (medium -> 25% reduction in downstream cost / latency), Confidence 0.6 (some telemetry), Effort = 4 dev-weeks for prefix-only canary. RICE (simple): (30k * 0.25 * 0.6) / 4 ~= 1125 (unitless). For full KV effort=12 -> score drops a lot.
Alex Rivera: Those numbers sound fine as a starting point. I'll export p50/p95 and request counts this afternoon and attach in the RICE doc. Also add customer list so we can prioritize accounts for canary opt-in.
Kim Nguyen: One more policy note: if canary causes >5% error-rate uptick or any data-correctness issue, auto-rollback. We should add a fallback policy that routes to plain serving runtime. Ops needs a toggle.
Jordan Lee: Agree. Also propose we include a soft-launch metric: "observed token-cost savings" over two weeks to validate unit economics before ramp.
Maria Chen: Ok action items: Samir -> make a short RICE table (prefix vs full) in the doc; Alex -> telemetry dump; Kim -> rollout/fallback checklist; Jordan -> customer canary list. Let's run async re-score by EOD Friday and decide Monday planning sync.
LaunchBot: Added card "Predictive Cache: prefix canary" to Roadmap board, owner=Samir, due=2026-04-03 :rocket:
Samir Patel: Thanks — I'll put the quick RICE table in the doc with assumptions and highlight the biggest unknowns (invalidation complexity, infra memory pressure).
Maria Chen: Great. If anyone has strong opinions about prioritizing QA time over additional feature polish for the canary, shout now. Otherwise we'll treat validation as high-priority. :eyes:
